legend: Greybox only: the brick joints (the vertical cracks in the rock) are schematic: the paint must not inherit masonry. The foot line: the pawn stands on the foot row (L+4, the face's row 4) in front of the contact shade and is never drawn on rock; faces cover rows 0-4, draw line 3 (rows below the lip row) so the pawn at row 4 draws over them. Day top = the ground one ramp step up (the measured meadow ground #74a65d -> #82b266); the lit band (2-3 px, its own meadow band #a9d082, or its own light-ground band #cee38a beside a low ground that #a9d082 would not clear by 25 luma) runs along fronts and backs only, never along a side wall, and never inside a side wall's lip; night by lighttables NIGHT_TOP (bands #2f5233 and #54773b). Side walls fill 14 of the flank tile's 16 px (two planes and a 2 px drop shade), come down flush to the lip corner and never stand proud of the top. A steep run (3+ one-column steps averaging over 1.25 rows) is one wall at an angle: its crease runs the slope, its foot is the next column's foot row.
description: The cliff system's piece table (pixel desk spec boards/pixel-spec/cliff-system.md; the game designer's rules boards/gdd/cliff-rules.md). One set for every level boundary. Each piece: its id, family, the case it serves (part, hand, k), its box in art px relative to the top-left of its anchor cell (x, y, w, h; 16 art px a cell, drawn at 3x), the cells it accounts for (relative to the anchor), its draw line (rows below the anchor row; the pieces sort by foot line, then class, then west to east) and the template zone it is painted in. Level 2 is level 1 through the one-step-paler map below (data, not paint). Picked by prototypes/places/src/bake/cliffsystem.mjs, which reads relief.mjs's parts.

tops.note: AD 2026-11-15: a top is its land's own ground one step up its own ramp, measured from the game's real ground fills (runs/cliff-system-greybox-fix-1/ground-colours.mjs); no land's colour is ever shifted to beat its neighbour. Only the meadow top is drawn (the 'top' piece): the level's raised ground is the one cliff terrain, whose top the land lays as meadow, and the other grounds a top can carry are not laid on a plateau yet. 'night' is the existing night step over the ground's night colour; null = the night ramp has no step there (the art director decides).

band.note: The top's lit band runs along fronts and backs only, never along a side wall (AD). It has two colours of its own, used by nothing else in the set (added to the set's palette through recipe.json paletteWiden; AD night ruling 2026-11-15): the meadow band #a9d082 (a day twin of the ramp's lightest #a8d082, 1 per channel), which clears the meadow ground by 44 luma, and the light-ground band #cee38a (a day twin of #cde38a), taken beside a low ground more than 162 luma (the band's 187 would clear it by under 25). By night lighttables NIGHT_TOP maps them: #a9d082 -> #2f5233, #cee38a -> #54773b; #a8d082 and #cde38a keep their own night entries (signed live art). groundLuma: the day luma of the measured fill of each terrain value.

pick.rule: s = hash(face world row, level) mod 6; t = world tile_x + s; letter = t mod 6; block = floor(t / 6); set = hash(block, face world row, level) mod 3

families.face: south face column: lip (row 0), rock rows 1-3, foot strip (row 4)
families.end: cap on the low cell beyond a run's end: the rock rounds under the lip; overhangs the run's last column by 4 px
families.corner: convex: the end cap that turns into a side wall; concave: the run's last column tucking behind a wall
families.diagonal: the slope rule (cliff-contour-1): a face column whose neighbour's lip is one row off draws its lip line through the half row between them; start and end are the two halves of a 2:1 slope (8 px down over the column), mid the 45 degree line; any number of steps from one
families.lean: a side wall moving one column over (cliff-contour-1): lean-{w,e} where it moves in toward the raised land going south (the upper wall's last cell, the lone lip, the cell under it), lean-out-{w,e} where it moves out (the upper wall's last cell, the corner, the lower wall's first cell); the lip and the rock lean over by a column at 45 degrees
families.steep: one column of a steep run (3+ steps of 1 column over that average more than 1.25 rows down): one side wall running down at an angle, edge-on rock in two planes with its crease on the slope, the lip stepping down along its top, the foot following; no strata, no cracks, no front slab per step
families.way: the way up: 2 columns, landing row above the lip, the stair cut through lip and rock
families.side: side walls: the lip seen from above on the ring cell, the rock edge-on on the flank cell
families.rim: the back rim: a lit edge on the ring cell and a drop shade on the low cell north of it; rim-{dr,dl}-{start,mid,end}: its one-row steps as slopes by the same half-row vertices as the faces' (cliff-contour-1)
families.top: the raised top, one level paler than the meadow
